task: Prospective multi-step ontology/objective/evidence-interface loops and path-dependence tests.

what_the_theorem_asserts.OSTC-T13: For regime morphisms f and g, transport is path independent iff every load-bearing coordinate satisfies a commuting coherence square, and T_{g o f} is isomorphic to T_g o T_f. Where a square fails, an object supported on the differing coordinate produces different obligations or terminals.

relation_to_EXEC_CM_01: EXEC-CM-01 tested the two-step case. This job extends to THREE-step chains and to CLOSED LOOPS, which the two-step case cannot reach: associativity of transport across three morphisms, and whether a declared round trip is the identity exactly when every square in the cycle commutes. No code is shared between the two jobs.

code_identity.checker_independence: The checker does not import the runner. Loop closure is recomputed by tracking each object around the cycle and comparing to its start, rather than by composing morphism tables; three-step associativity is recomputed by explicit left/right grouping over objects rather than over tables.

comparator_identity.endpoint_only_donor: A donor that declares two paths equivalent whenever their endpoint regimes match, ignoring the route taken. T13 says path dependence is real, so this donor MUST be observed to fail -- admitting at least one pair of same-endpoint routes that transport differently. A donor that never fails would mean the enumeration contains no genuine path dependence and cannot test the theorem.

information_and_tool_access.runner: declared grid only; no network, no model calls

independent_unit: The (chain-or-loop, declared-transport) cell. Objects inside a cell are exhaustively enumerated, not sampled.

estimands.three_step_associativity: Over all three-morphism chains: does (h o g) o f transport every object identically to h o (g o f), with zero exceptions?
estimands.loop_biconditional: Over all closed loops: is (round trip is the identity on every object) exactly equivalent to (every square in the cycle commutes), checked in both directions?
estimands.path_dependence_is_real: Do path-dependent cases actually occur? A grid in which every route agrees cannot test path dependence and is recorded as a negative.
estimands.donor_fails: Does the endpoint-only donor admit at least one same-endpoint route pair that transports differently?

multiplicity: No hypothesis test; universal and existence claims over total enumeration.
positive_conditions: loop biconditional holds with zero exceptions in both directions
path-dependent cases occur (the theorem is testable on this grid)
the endpoint-only donor fails at least once
negative_conditions: any three-step chain where the two groupings disagree
any loop where identity-round-trip and all-squares-commute come apart in either direction
no path-dependent case exists in the grid, making the theorem vacuous here
the endpoint-only donor never fails, which means the same thing
cannot_check_conditions: grid not exhausted within the wallclock bound

checker_and_authority_owner.independence_boundary: Two implementations inside one programme; not external adjudication.

constitutional_note: May confirm, refute or narrow an instantiation. May not redesign a theorem, move a gate, weaken a comparator, hide a negative, or rewrite theory after outcome access.
